questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Famous sisters in British politics
How to stop sisters from arguing
Why younger sisters are spoiled
The relationship between sisters and some common beliefs about it
questions.why: They discuss the connection between sisters, hear from three Irish sisters and a psychotherapist.

questions.q: How does Georgie get on with her sister?
options: Very well now as adults, though they didn't before
They have always got on very well
They rarely speak to each other
They argue much more now than they did when they were children
questions.why: Georgie says they didn't used to get on, but now that they're adults they get on well.

questions.q: What do we learn about presenter Nuala McGovern and her sisters?
options: All three sisters now work together as journalists for the BBC in London
Nuala is the oldest of the three
Nuala moved abroad for work, while her sisters stayed in Ireland
Her sisters live in New York
questions.why: Nuala moved to New York then London to work, while her two sisters stayed in Ireland.

questions.q: What was Nuala a little worried about?
options: The video call not working
What her sisters might say about her on the radio
Her sisters arguing on air
Forgetting her sisters' names in front of the listeners
questions.why: Georgie says Nuala was a little worried what her sisters would say about her.

questions.q: How does Eileen describe the sisters' relationship?
options: Difficult but improving
Very connected, and they get on well
Distant, because they live in different countries
Competitive, like a game
questions.why: Eileen says 'Very connected… we do get on very well'.

options: Shy and quiet
Bossy and spoiled
Independent and liking to be in control
The peacemaker who stops the family from arguing
questions.why: Vera says Nuala marches to her own drum, agrees she's independent and likes to control the situation.

questions.q: What does psychotherapist Jennifer Gledhill say about stereotypes like the 'bossy older sister'?
options: They are true in most families
They only apply to large families
They are mostly true for brothers, but they don't really apply to sisters
People like labels, but science has found no proof of these roles
questions.why: She says we love giving people labels, but scientists find no proof of these roles.

questions.q: Why does Georgie disagree with the stereotypes?
options: In her family, the younger sister is the bossy one
She has no sisters
She is the bossy older sister and always tells her sister what to do
Her sister is the peacemaker
questions.why: She says the older sister is meant to be bossy, 'but my younger sister is the bossy one'.
